issue: For a JP route, `directionsMinutes` returns ONLY the transit `durationSecs` (travel.js:181-185) with no fallback comparison against drive time — unlike the pre-existing `directionsMinutesGoogle` path (travel.js:136-146) which explicitly documents ('never-late bias: we don't yet know the user's mode, so assume the slower so we never under-estimate', travel.js:127-128) and implements `MAX(transit, drive)`. This removes the codebase's own documented never-late safety margin specifically for JP users. Worse, `transit.js`'s `parseTransitPlan` (transit.js:37-53) takes `best.durationSecs` directly from the transit.ls8h.com response without adding `accessWalkSecs` (the walk from the origin to the departure platform) — the committed fixture proves this: journey[0]'s leg-level `departureSecs` (83280) equals the journey-level `departureSecs` (83280) even though `accessWalkSecs:61` is a separate sibling field, and `durationSecs:1029` = leg duration(900) + `egressWalkSecs`(129) only, i.e. the 61s walk-to-station is silently dropped from the number every caller treats as 'total travel time'. Combined, a JP user's leave-time can be computed shorter than reality by (accessWalkSecs + the removed never-late margin), directly threatening the product's core 'call me before I must leave' promise for exactly the population (JP) this PR optimizes for.
evidence: .vcsdd/features/life-manager-cost-connect-reliability/evidence/fixtures/transit-plan-tokyo-shinjuku.json:1 — journeys[0]: {"departureSecs":83280,"arrivalSecs":84309,"durationSecs":1029, legs:[{"departureSecs":83280,"arrivalSecs":84180}], "accessWalkSecs":61,"egressWalkSecs":129} — 84309-83280=1029=900(leg)+129(egress), with accessWalkSecs(61) present but mathematically absent from durationSecs. apps/life-call/lib/travel.js:181-185: `if (parsed && parsed.durationSecs != null) return minutesFromSeconds(parsed.durationSecs);` returns immediately, never calling `google()`/MAX for the JP branch.
fix: In `parseTransitPlan` (transit.js), add `accessWalkSecs` (and any transfer walk legs) into the returned `durationSecs` so it represents true origin-to-destination time. In `directionsMinutes`'s JP branch, either keep a bounded safety margin (e.g. +N% or the historical drive-time comparison as an upper sanity bound) consistent with the codebase's own documented never-late philosophy, rather than trusting a single unofficial third-party schedule number verbatim.
